title: Calendar Math: Adding Months Safely
hints: Let `Calendar` do date math — never add seconds for months.
Configure a Gregorian calendar and `DateFormatter` with UTC and `en_US_POSIX`.
jsBridge: Adding "one month" with `Calendar.date(byAdding: .month, …)` clamps Jan 31 → Feb 28/29. JS `Date` arithmetic overflows into March. Calendars are a Foundation strength, and JS only now gets `Temporal`.

compass.q: `d.setMonth(d.getMonth() + 1)` on Jan 31 gives March 3 in JS. What does `Calendar` give, and why?
DST transitions: is adding 1 day the same as adding 24 hours? When does it differ?
`Calendar` arithmetic vs `TimeInterval` arithmetic: which for "same time tomorrow"?
Subscription renewal dates: whose calendar and time zone decides?
